---
title: "Readings — How sequencers read DNA"
---

The platform papers are worth reading as primary sources: each one is an argument for a
particular trade-off, and those trade-offs are still what you choose between today.

## The platforms

**Sanger F, Nicklen S, Coulson AR (1977).** *DNA sequencing with chain-terminating
inhibitors.* PNAS 74:5463–5467.
[doi:10.1073/pnas.74.12.5463](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.74.12.5463) — **start here**

> Short, and the baseline for everything after it. Note what it requires: one template
> species, one primer. Every design decision in massively parallel sequencing follows from
> removing that requirement.

**Bentley DR, et al. (2008).** *Accurate whole human genome sequencing using reversible
terminator chemistry.* Nature 456:53–59.
[doi:10.1038/nature07517](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature07517) — **start here**

> The Illumina system as first described: bridge amplification, reversible terminators,
> paired ends. Read the methods for the library prep, and notice how little has changed.

**Drmanac R, et al. (2010).** *Human genome sequencing using unchained base reads on
self-assembling DNA nanoarrays.* Science 327:78–81.
[doi:10.1126/science.1181498](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1181498)

> DNA nanoballs: amplify a circle by rolling circle instead of a cluster by PCR. The origin
> of what is now DNBSEQ/MGI, and a good illustration that "amplify the library on a surface"
> has more than one solution.

**Eid J, et al. (2009).** *Real-time DNA sequencing from single polymerase molecules.*
Science 323:133–138. [doi:10.1126/science.1162986](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1162986)

> Watching one polymerase work. Skim the optics; the part that matters for library design is
> the zero-mode waveguide and what it implies about input molecule quality.

**Wenger AM, et al. (2019).** *Accurate circular consensus long-read sequencing improves
variant detection and assembly of a human genome.* Nature Biotechnology 37:1155–1162.
[doi:10.1038/s41587-019-0217-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-019-0217-9)

> How HiFi works: trade insert length for passes, and get accuracy out of repetition. This is
> the paper that made long reads trustworthy for variant calling.

**Arslan S, et al. (2023).** *Sequencing by avidity enables high accuracy with low reagent
consumption.* Nature Biotechnology 42:132–138.
[doi:10.1038/s41587-023-01750-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-023-01750-7)

> Element's AVITI. Worth reading for the idea of separating binding from incorporation —
> a genuinely different way to get a strong signal.

**Jain M, Olsen HE, Paten B, Akeson M (2016).** *The Oxford Nanopore MinION: delivery of
nanopore sequencing to the genomics community.* Genome Biology 17:239.
[doi:10.1186/s13059-016-1103-0](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-1103-0)

> A readable introduction to how the pore and the motor protein work.

**Jain M, et al. (2018).** *Nanopore sequencing and assembly of a human genome with
ultra-long reads.* Nature Biotechnology 36:338–345.
[doi:10.1038/nbt.4060](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4060)

> What ultra-long reads take: the library prep is mostly an exercise in not shearing the DNA.
> Read it as a lesson in sample handling.

**Wang Y, Zhao Y, Bollas A, Wang Y, Au KF (2021).** *Nanopore sequencing technology,
bioinformatics and applications.* Nature Biotechnology 39:1348–1365.
[doi:10.1038/s41587-021-01108-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-021-01108-x)

> A review to dip into rather than read through — use it for the kit chemistry and the
> error-profile discussion.

## Indexes and what goes wrong with them

**Kircher M, Sawyer S, Meyer M (2011).** *Double indexing overcomes inaccuracies in multiplex
sequencing on the Illumina platform.* Nucleic Acids Research 40:e3.
[doi:10.1093/nar/gkr771](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkr771)

> Why one index is not enough. The argument here is the reason dual indexing is standard.

**Costello M, et al. (2018).** *Characterization and remediation of sample index swaps by
non-redundant dual indexing on massively parallel sequencing platforms.* BMC Genomics 19:332.
[doi:10.1186/s12864-018-4703-0](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12864-018-4703-0)

> Index hopping measured, and the fix that follows from it. Read this before pooling anything
> precious with cheap index sets.

## Reference material to keep open

- **[NGS 101](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/)** — each protocol names its platform
  and shows the finished construct with the reads marked on it.
- **Illumina's adapter and index sequence documentation** — the authoritative list of what
  P5, P7, the read primers and the index sets actually are, and which instruments use the
  forward-strand or reverse-complement i5 workflow. Check the current version: reagent kits
  change this.
- **Your sequencing facility's run-setup form** — a surprisingly good teaching document. It
  asks exactly the questions this deck is about: read lengths, index lengths, custom primers,
  PhiX fraction, loading concentration.

## If you want to go further

- Nanopore's **adaptive sampling**, and what it means for enrichment steps that used to be
  wet-lab work.
- **Protein sequencing** at the single-molecule level, which borrows directly from these
  ideas and may be where the field goes next.
